name: LUXEMBOURG

flag.title: Grand Duchy Flag
flag.note: Red, white & light blue — three stripes

lead: Luxembourg is tiny. You could drive across it in under an hour. It has fairy-tale castles, deep forests, and one of Earth's highest living standards. It sits between France, Belgium, and Germany.

facts.label: High point
facts.sub: A gentle Ardennes hilltop in north

geo: Hills, forests, and sandstone gorges (deep, narrow valleys) cover the Ardennes region in the north. The south is gentler farmland that locals call 'the Good Land'.
The Moselle River forms the border with Germany, lined with steep vineyards (grape farms). Luxembourg City stands on rocky cliffs above two rivers, the Alzette and the Pétrusse.
animals: Red deer, wild boar, and shy otters live in the Ardennes forests. Beavers came back after two centuries away.
Kingfishers flash blue over the Moselle. Greater horseshoe bats sleep in the old fortress caves under Luxembourg City.
culture: Luxembourg has three official languages. People speak Luxembourgish at home and use French for official papers. Early school lessons are in German.
The national dish is smoked pork collar with broad beans. The country makes 15 million bottles of Moselle wine a year. The Schueberfouer funfair has run every autumn since 1340.
history: Luxembourg's clifftop fortress, built over 400 years, was called 'the Gibraltar of the North', after a famous rock fortress. In 1867, great powers declared Luxembourg permanently neutral (on no side in wars), so it was torn down.

Luxembourg was occupied twice in the World Wars. The Battle of the Bulge, a huge World War II fight, tore through its hills in 1944–45. Later it helped found what became the European Union, a group of countries that work together.
wows: Luxembourg City hosts three big EU offices, more than any capital outside Brussels.
Luxembourg has the highest GDP (money earned) per person in the EU.
Nearly 47% of residents were born abroad, one of the most mixed countries in the world.
220,000 workers travel in from three countries to work every day.
In 2020, all buses, trains, and trams became free for everyone.
The Müllerthal region's mossy sandstone mazes earned it the nickname 'Little Switzerland'.
Luxembourg is the world's only Grand Duchy, a country ruled by a grand duke.

myths.fact: Belgium has a province named Luxembourg. It is a different place next door.
Many are smaller, such as Vatican City, Monaco, San Marino, and Malta.
